diagrams.title: Cutaneous Lupus Classification
diagrams.subtitle: Morphologic subtype predicts scarring behavior and systemic association

children.name: Localized ACLE
children.detail: Malar/butterfly eruption; nasolabial sparing supports lupus over DM or rosacea.

children.name: Generalized ACLE
children.detail: Symmetric photodistributed macules/papules; severe bullous/TEN-like variants are uncommon.

children.name: Acute CLE (ACLE)
children.detail: Transient, photosensitive, non-scarring; usually associated with active SLE.

children.name: Annular/polycyclic
children.detail: Raised scaly edge with central clearing.

children.name: Papulosquamous
children.detail: Psoriasiform or eczematous plaques in a photodistribution.

children.name: Subacute CLE (SCLE)
children.detail: Highly photosensitive, non-scarring; anti-Ro/SSA common; drug induction is important.

children.name: Discoid LE
children.detail: Localized or generalized; follicular plugging, scarring, dyspigmentation and alopecia.

children.name: Tumid LE
children.detail: Smooth edematous plaques without epidermal change or scarring.

children.name: Other variants
children.detail: Hypertrophic, mucosal, lichenoid overlap and other less common patterns.

children.name: Chronic CLE (CCLE)
children.detail: Greater risk of permanent damage; systemic risk varies by subtype.

root.name: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus
root.detail: Clinicopathologic correlation is required; histology can overlap.

diagrams.title: CLE Morphology and Biopsy Strategy
diagrams.subtitle: Choose the lesion and specimen that answer the diagnostic question

steps.prompt: Is the dominant lesion superficial/epidermal, smooth-edematous, deep, or ulcerative?
Biopsy the active erythematous/scaly edge, including follicles
steps.detail: H&E may show interface dermatitis, follicular plugging, thickened basement membrane, periadnexal inflammation, mucin, and later scarring. Sample scalp early if distinguishing active DLE from burnt-out scarring alopecia.

steps.prompt: Biopsy a fresh active plaque and correlate with distribution
steps.detail: ACLE and SCLE may show superficial interface dermatitis; histology alone may not subtype disease or distinguish DM. Medication history and morphology remain essential.

steps.prompt: Biopsy the center/active portion of a fully developed smooth plaque
steps.detail: Expected pattern: dense perivascular/periadnexal lymphocytes and abundant dermal mucin with minimal or absent epidermal/interface change. Consider Jessner infiltrate and polymorphous light eruption.

steps.prompt: Use a deep punch/incisional biopsy that captures subcutis
steps.detail: Lobular lymphocytic panniculitis, hyaline fat necrosis, lymphoid aggregates, and mucin support lupus panniculitis. Exclude subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma when atypical.

steps.prompt: Could this be infection, vasculitis/vasculopathy, immunobullous disease, drug reaction, or malignancy?

steps.detail: H&E from lesional edge; tissue cultures/stains if infection is plausible; perilesional tissue in appropriate transport medium for DIF if immunobullous disease is considered. Depth should match suspected vessel/panniculus involvement.

steps.prompt: Biopsy the active edge and reassess systemic disease
steps.detail: Ulceration is not a routine feature of most CLE subtypes; investigate vasculitis, antiphospholipid vasculopathy, pyoderma gangrenosum, infection, calciphylaxis, and malignancy.

diagrams.title: CLE Histopathology by Clinical Subtype
diagrams.subtitle: Histology is supportive; lesion age, treatment, and biopsy site alter the pattern

children.name: ACLE
children.detail: Usually relatively superficial vacuolar interface dermatitis with dyskeratotic keratinocytes and dermal mucin.

children.name: SCLE
children.detail: Interface dermatitis with superficial perivascular inflammation; may be difficult to distinguish from ACLE, DM, or lichenoid drug reaction.

children.name: DLE
children.detail: More prominent follicular plugging, basement-membrane thickening, superficial/deep perivascular and periadnexal inflammation, mucin, and late scarring.

children.name: Tumid lupus
children.detail: Dense superficial/deep perivascular and periadnexal lymphocytes with abundant mucin and little/no interface change.

children.name: Lupus panniculitis
children.detail: Lobular lymphocytic panniculitis, hyaline fat necrosis, lymphoid aggregates, mucin, and possible overlying DLE.

children.name: Direct immunofluorescence
children.detail: Granular immunoreactants at the dermoepidermal junction can support lupus but are neither perfectly sensitive nor specific; use the correct specimen and clinical context.
